statement: Build a one-page website for Brew Lab, a cafe in Indiranagar, Bengaluru, that shows the menu, opening hours and location, lets visitors pre-order for pickup, and features a large photo gallery of the cafe and a detailed story section for each of its three coffee farms.
audience: Local customers and visitors in Indiranagar, Bengaluru, mostly on phones, who want to check the menu and hours, find the cafe, pre-order for pickup, and learn where the coffee comes from.
standards: One HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
Low cost: no paid services and no backend; gallery images lazy-load.
No invented facts: any detail not in the brief appears as a visibly marked placeholder.
rules: Never invent prices, hours, address, phone numbers, farm names, farm facts or photos; use marked placeholders.
Every placeholder is visibly labelled so it cannot be mistaken for real content.
Keep everything the brief asks for: menu, hours, location, pre-order for pickup, large photo gallery, and detailed stories for all three farms.
Pre-order must work without a server: it builds an order summary and hands it off to a destination that is a marked placeholder.
done_when: The site is a single HTML file with inline CSS and JS and needs no build step.
The page names Brew Lab and Indiranagar, Bengaluru, and has navigation links that jump to each section.
A menu section lists items grouped by category, with unknown prices marked as placeholders.
An hours section lists all seven days, marked as placeholder where unknown.
A location section shows the address (placeholder if unknown) and an embedded map or map link for Indiranagar, Bengaluru.
A pre-order for pickup form lets the visitor choose menu items and quantities, enter name, phone and pickup time, see a running total, and submit to a marked placeholder destination.
A photo gallery section has at least 12 image slots in a responsive grid with a lightbox, alt text on every image, and placeholder images clearly marked.
Three separate farm story sections each have a name, location, multi-paragraph story and key details (such as altitude, variety, process), all marked as placeholders where unknown.
The file has a viewport meta tag and responsive CSS so it works on a phone-width screen.
Every placeholder in the file is visibly marked as a placeholder.
open_inputs: Street address and map pin for the cafe
Phone number and/or WhatsApp or email for receiving pre-orders
Pickup time rules (slot length, lead time)
Names, locations and stories of the three coffee farms
Farm photos and key details (altitude, variety, process)
